usageNotes: Called by the Proxmox automated installer (proxmox-auto-install-assistant) when a new machine boots from an auto-install ISO and fetches its answer file via HTTP — it is not typically called directly by administrators. The installer POSTs system-discovery data (DMI hardware info, ISO metadata, detected network interfaces, and product config) and receives back a fully-resolved answer-file object that governs disk setup, network, credentials, and post-install hooks for that specific machine. Authentication uses specialized bearer tokens (not standard API tokens), and the endpoint is world-accessible by design so the booting machine can reach it without pre-enrolled credentials.

examples.summary: PVE node fetches its answer file during unattended installation

tips: This endpoint is consumed by the installer at boot time, not by admin tooling — use it to verify what answer file a specific machine would receive before deploying.
The bearer token scheme is separate from normal PDM API tokens; configure it in the PDM auto-install settings before pointing ISOs at the PDM answer server.
The response's 'global.fqdn' field can be set to 'from-dhcp' so each machine self-registers its hostname rather than receiving a hardcoded one.
Use 'disk-setup.filter' with udev properties (e.g. ID_BUS=ata, ID_SERIAL) to target specific disks without listing them by name, which is safer across heterogeneous hardware.
Set 'post-installation-webhook' to call back your provisioning system after install completes so you can trigger Ansible/Salt runs or update your CMDB automatically.
